idiom_name: hand-written test_* functions with Unity's setUp()/tearDown() callbacks and TEST_ASSERT_* macros
implementation_notes: C has no test facility of its own: the three beats are hand-placed inside each test function, and the runner only sees the functions you register explicitly (Unity's RUN_TEST list, or the list a generator produces from the test_/spec_ naming convention). Unity supplies the assertion vocabulary - TEST_ASSERT_EQUAL_INT, TEST_ASSERT_TRUE - plus optional per-file setUp()/tearDown() callbacks that run around every test, so shared cleanup belongs there while test-specific state stays in the function; a fixture struct initialised in setUp keeps the arrange beat from swamping the body.
pitfalls: Unity runs what you register: a test function missing from the RUN_TEST list still compiles and silently never executes, so generated runners or a checklist are the safety net.

C has no exceptions - the act beat signals failure through return codes and out-parameters, so the test must check them before the assert beat reads state, or the assertion verifies stale values and passes.

setUp()/tearDown() are per test file and must exist (even empty) when the runner expects them, or the executable fails to link; shared fixtures must be arranged per file, because each test file is linked as its own executable.
